 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. World number one Alexander Zverev began the WTA Finals with a 6-4, 6-4 victory over debutant Rafael Jódar in Turin on Sunday.
 German Zverev, who won this title in 2018 and 2021, is coming off his best year having taken his maiden Grand Slam titles in Paris and New York.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The 29-year-old top seed had the honour of opening the round-robin singles event and immediately took charge of the John McEnroe group thanks to 10 aces and 86% of first serve points won.
 Spaniard Jódar was making his debut at the end-of-season championship after the injury pull-out of home hero Jannik Sinner opened the door to the tournament for the best eight men's tennis players.
 Jódar, 20, only turned professional at the start of the year and won in Morocco in April before finishing as runner-up in Washington and at the Shanghai Masters.
 But his rapid ascent this season was checked by Zverev seizing a third break point with a superb passing shot for 4-3 in the first set.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Jódar had break points at 5-4, but Zverev's booming serve on the indoor hard-court saved him.
 Zverev broke for 2-1 in the second after a frustrated Jódar hit the net after the German's shot had come off the net-cord.
 US third seed Ben Shelton takes on French sixth seed Arthur Fils in the second group match later on Sunday.
 Second seed Carlos Alcaraz starts off the Ivan Lendl group against Frances Tiafoe on Monday before Daniel Medvedev faces Flavio Cobolli.
